title: Finitely generated Z-algebras are G-rings
statement: Every finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra, i.e. every commutative ring $R$ generated as a ring by finitely many elements, is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] (Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Proposition Tag 07PX, items (3) and (5), using Proposition Tag 07PV).

source.place: Proposition Tag 07PX (proposition-ubiquity-G-ring, line 12652), items (3) ($\mathbf Z$, a Dedekind domain of characteristic zero whose completions at maximal ideals are discrete valuation rings) and (5) (finite type ring extensions, Proposition Tag 07PV proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring)

proof.text: The canonical map $\mathbf Z\to R$ exhibits $R$ as a finite type $\mathbf Z$-algebra: if $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ generate $R$ as a ring, the map $\mathbf Z[X_1,\ldots,X_n]\to R$ sending $X_i$ to $r_i$ is surjective.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07PX proof, item (5), specialized to a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra

proof.text: By the G-ring fact for $\mathbf Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-z-g-ring] and the finite-type permanence proposition [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring], this finite type $\mathbf Z$-algebra is a G-ring.
